header.running_head: Enduring Hunger when Inviting People Towards Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ

blocks.text: The Hunger Endured by Hadhrat Asmaa bint Abi Bakr (RA)

Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) the daughter of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) says, "I was once in the land in the Banu Nadheer district that Rasulullaah ﷺ had apportioned to Hadhrat Abu Salma (RA) and (my husband) Hadhrat Zubayr (RA). Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) had left with Rasulullaah ﷺ on a journey. Our neighbour was a Jew who had then slaughtered a goat and cooked it. When I smelt the aroma, I experienced a desire like I never felt before. At that time, I was expecting my daughter Khadeeja and could not bear the desire. I then went to the Jewish woman to ask for some fire with the hope that she would give me some to eat because I really had no need for the fire. When I smelt the aroma (from inside the house) and saw the food, my desire grew even more intense and extinguished the fire (she had given me). I then returned a second time to ask for fire and again a third time. (When she did not give me anything) I eventually sat down to cry and prayed to Allaah. When the Jewish lady's husband returned, he asked her, 'Has anyone been to you?' 'Yes,' she replied, 'an Arab lady came to ask for some fire.' He said, 'I shall never eat the food until you send some to her.' A plate of food was then sent to me. There was nothing on earth that I enjoyed more than that meal."[^2]
The Hunger Endured by the Sahabah (RA) in General
The Extreme Hunger and Cold that the Sahabah (RA) Suffered During the Battle of Khandaq

The son of a Sahabi called Abu Jihaad (RA) once told him, "Dear father! You have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ and enjoyed his company." The son then went on to describe the many feats that he would have carried out had he seen Rasulullaah ﷺ. His father said, "Fear Allaah and continue doing what is correct. I swear by the Being Who controls my life that we experienced a time with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Khandaq when Rasulullaah ﷺ announced, 'The person who will go and gather intelligence about the enemy, Allaah shall make him my companion on the Day of Qiyaamah.' No one stood up (to volunteer) because of the intense hunger and cold that we were suffering. Eventually (when no one responded), Rasulullaah ﷺ announced the third time, 'O Hudhayfa (come forward for the task).'"[^3] The detailed Hadith of Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) will Insha Allaah be quoted in the chapter discussing the extreme cold the Sahabah
